chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about wounds, and he said: “A woman’s wound is like a man’s wound until it reaches one-third of the diyah. Then, when it reaches one-third of the diyah equally, a man’s wound is made double in comparison to a woman’s wound. And the tooth of a woman and the tooth of a man are equal.”
And he said: “If a man were to kill his wife intentionally, and the woman’s family wanted to kill the man, they would return half of the diyah to the man’s family and then kill him.”
He said: And I asked him about a woman who killed a man. He said: “She is killed for him, and her family does not have to pay anything.”

key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: financial compensation paid for homicide or bodily injury
key_terms.الْجِرَاحَاتِ: bodily wounds or injuries for which legal compensation is assessed
key_terms.تُقْتَلُ بِهِ: she is subject to retaliatory execution for killing him
key_terms.ثُلُثَ: one-third, the threshold mentioned for change in compensation ruling
key_terms.جِرَاحَةُ: a wound or injury in the legal sense
key_terms.سِنُّ: a tooth, specifically mentioned as equal between man and woman

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings on diyah and qisas between men and women in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith presents legal rulings concerning bodily injury compensation and retaliatory punishment between men and women. It outlines the point at which compensation differs, affirms equality in the case of a tooth, and explains the rule of qisas in cases where a husband kills his wife or a woman kills a man.
